candidates.source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — corporate site (payments processor for Slovenian banking sector)
candidates.why_relevant: Bankart is the central Slovenian card/payments processor, founded 1997 by the majority of SI banks; it runs card issuing/acquiring processing, ATM and POS network management, the payment gateway, PSD2/open banking services, and operates the national SEPA and instant-payment systems. Its site is the single densest public trace of who owns and supplies SI payments infrastructure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled crawl of site sections (podjetje, storitve, novice) + PDF harvesting from /wp-content/uploads
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on card processing providers
queries_used: procesiranje kartic Slovenija ponudnik plačilne platforme banka
Bankart novice sporočila za javnost nova plačilna platforma projekt 2025

candidates.source_name: Bankart — 'Opis plačilnih sistemov za procesiranje SEPA transakcij' PDF series (SIMP-PS / BIPS scheme descriptions)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative, versioned scheme documentation for the SIMP-PS (SEPA) and BIPS (Bankart Instant Payment System) systems, including ISO 20022 message rules, participants and Bank of Slovenia authorisation. Re-issued periodically, so successive versions reveal infrastructure and participant change over time.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Diff successive dated PDF versions; extract participant lists and system names
queries_used: Slovenia SEPA instant payments SIMP-PS Bankart ISO 20022 implementation vendor

candidates.source_name: Bankart — Flik product pages and merchant onboarding documentation
candidates.why_relevant: Flik is the Slovenian instant-payment/mobile scheme built on Bankart's instant rails. Product pages plus the merchant onboarding PDFs (payment gateway, Flik e-commerce, Flik POS) expose the technical integration stack, alias/QR/NFC capability and the acquirer-merchant chain — a rare public description of a national scheme's implementation detail.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch product pages and linked PDFs; track version numbers in filenames
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on Flik technology partner
queries_used: Flik takojšnja plačila Bankart tehnološki partner rešitev

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Upravljavci plačilnih sistemov (payment system operators)
candidates.why_relevant: Regulator's list of authorised payment system operators — the definitive statement of which entities legally run SI payment infrastructure (e.g. Bankart for SIMP-PS/BIPS). Ownership and authorisation changes here are leading indicators of infrastructure change.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic snapshot + diff of register pages
queries_used: Banka Slovenije plačilni sistemi nadzor register upravljavci plačilnih sistemov

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Register subjektov nadzora (supervised entities: payment institutions, EMIs, PISP/AISP)
candidates.why_relevant: Enumerates payment institutions, e-money institutions and account information/payment initiation providers licensed in SI — the entry list for non-bank payments players (e.g. Paywiser) that buy or build issuing/processing stacks.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Register scrape + diff; join with company registry data
candidates.discovered_via_method: regulator site navigation from operator register
queries_used: Banka Slovenije plačilni sistemi nadzor register upravljavci plačilnih sistemov

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Poročanje upravljavcev plačilnih sistemov / poročilo o delovanju plačilnega sistema
candidates.why_relevant: Reporting instructions and templates for payment system operators reveal what infrastructure metrics exist (availability, incidents, volumes) and where derived statistics on SI payment systems can be obtained — useful for sizing and reliability comparisons between infrastructures.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch reporting instructions and any published aggregate statistics
queries_used: Banka Slovenije plačilni sistemi nadzor register upravljavci plačilnih sistemov

candidates.source_name: FinTech Futures — Bankart/Nets Slovenian payments central infrastructure story
candidates.why_relevant: Documents the vendor selection behind Slovenia's central SCT / SCT Inst infrastructure (Nets as technology supplier to Bankart). This is exactly the kind of go-live/vendor-award trace the cell targets, and FinTech Futures covers such awards across CEE consistently.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-filtered RSS/site search monitoring for 'Slovenia', 'Bankart', 'Flik', vendor names
candidates.discovered_via_method: English vendor search snowballed to trade press
queries_used: Bankart card processing platform vendor OpenWay Way4 OR Nets OR TSYS Slovenia

negative_findings.description: No public announcement was found naming a specific card issuing/acquiring platform vendor behind Bankart's card processing (e.g. OpenWay Way4, TSYS, Tietoevry). Only the SEPA/instant central infrastructure has a named external supplier (Nets) in the sources found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor searches returned generic vendor marketing pages plus one Bankart–Nets infrastructure story; no SI card-platform reference page surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The identity of the card management system under Slovenia's national processor is the single most valuable unknown for this cell; its absence must not be filled by assumption.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenia-specific Visa or Mastercard processor certification or principal-membership announcement was found for 2025-2026 in open search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Scheme searches returned only generic global licensing/certification guidance pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme certification announcements were assumed to be a primary public trace for this cell; they appear to be published mostly via scheme directories rather than press releases, shifting collection toward directory scraping.

negative_findings.description: Slovenian-language terminology for tokenisation is thin: searches on tokenizacija/žetoniziranje kartic produced no dedicated SI vendor or bank technical page in this pass; SI sources use English terms or describe the capability functionally (mobilno kartično plačevanje, digitalna denarnica).
negative_findings.result_summary: Tokenisation as a named local-language concept has no distinct SI source footprint found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Tokenisation supplier identity (scheme TSP vs. processor-hosted) stays unmapped for SI, and the local glossary lacks a reliable query term for it.

negative_findings.description: A reference surfaced to the historical 'Transact-EON' authorisation network linking Bankart, Banka Koper and Plasis, and to legacy SI card brands (Activa, Karanta). No current authoritative page was located for these.
negative_findings.result_summary: Mentioned only in a low-quality secondary aggregation; historical status unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Legacy switch/brand names are useful archival query terms for reconstructing SI switching history but must be treated as unverified until a primary source is found.

negative_findings.description: Euronet is named by a secondary source as an acquiring-processing provider in Slovenia alongside Bankart and Cetis, but no Euronet Slovenia acquiring/processing page was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Actor plausible but not sourced to a primary page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Euronet is a significant ATM/acquiring processor regionally; leaving it unmapped would understate the competitive set.

negative_findings.description: Margento and Halcom, both Slovenian payment-technology names, returned no payments-platform or tokenisation evidence under the combined query used.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query conflated three companies; only Paywiser returned substantive results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Halcom (e-banking/qualified certificates) and Margento (mobile payments) are plausible SI payments-adjacent vendors that remain unassessed; they need dedicated single-entity queries.

coverage_gaps.description: The card management / issuing platform layer under Bankart and under SI banks is unmapped — no named CMS, switch, HSM or tokenisation supplier identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Target Bankart annual reports via AJPES, Bankart job postings (technology stack signals), procurement notices, and vendor-side reference pages (OpenWay, Tietoevry, Nexi/SIA, Euronet, BPC, Compass Plus) filtered on Slovenia.

coverage_gaps.description: No recruitment/job-posting sources were collected, though these are among the most reliable public indicators of which payment platforms an organisation actually operates.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add SI job boards (mojedelo.com, zaposlitev.net, LinkedIn Jobs SI) with queries on platform names and roles (kartično poslovanje, plačilni sistemi, ISO 20022, Way4, Base24).

coverage_gaps.description: Conference and industry-association sources for SI payments (Bančni vestnik, Združenje bank Slovenije, ICT/payments conferences) were not covered; these carry vendor presentations naming implementations.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout Združenje bank Slovenije (zbs-giz.si), Bančni vestnik archives, and SI/regional payments conference agendas for vendor speaker slots.

coverage_gaps.description: Cross-border consolidation (Nexi Croatia owning Nexi Slovenija; NLB's regional footprint) means SI vendor facts often appear only in HR/RS/BA sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend queries into hr/sr language sources for the same processing entities and treat regional processor announcements as SI-relevant.

brief: Slovenia's payments vendor layer is unusually concentrated: Bankart d.o.o., bank-owned since 1997, is simultaneously the national card issuing/acquiring processor, the ATM/POS estate manager, the payment gateway and PSD2 operator, and the Bank of Slovenia-authorised operator of the SIMP-PS (SEPA) and BIPS (instant) systems on which the Flik scheme rides — making bankart.si plus the Banka Slovenije registers the two anchor sources for this cell. The second visible tier is foreign-owned and traceable mainly through corporate registries rather than press releases: Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. (formerly Intesa Sanpaolo Card, then Nets CEE) processes cards from Ljubljana, and Nets is documented as the technology supplier behind Bankart's central SCT/SCT Inst infrastructure. Below the processor tier, evidence gets indirect — acquirer merchant pages and general-terms PDFs, integrator case studies (SRC's PSD2 platform), core-banking suppliers (HRC/Hibis) and the eNaročanje procurement portal are the practical routes to supplier identity. The single most important unknown is the card management/switch/tokenisation platform actually running inside Bankart and the SI banks: no public source found in this pass names it, and Visa/Mastercard certification news for Slovenia appears to live in scheme partner directories rather than announcements.
